depth_findings.text: AcquireLease for a thread scope accepts any scope_id from any user with a sandbox bearer and never checks it against session-core's thread ownership, so a user can create workspace rows and blobs under another user's thread id in the same org. S5 refuses to erase a shared id, which also blocks the victim's own erase. The ownership check belongs in acquireThread before default-on.

The blob prefix cas/thread/<org>/<thread>/ carries no owner, and blobs are uploaded before their rows exist, so a non-owner erase could remove a first write whose header is not yet there. An owner-scoped prefix or an erasing tombstone is needed.

Rows are erased before blobs, so a blob-delete failure leaves unreachable blobs with no record to retry from. A durable erasure tombstone or retry queue is needed before default-on for GDPR completeness.

With SANDBOX_MANAGER_THREAD_WORKSPACE off, neither the sweeper nor DELETE runs, so rows and blobs written while it was on are neither expired nor erasable after a rollback. A retention-only path is needed before default-on.

The WS17 thread-delete hook is not wired: session-core's delete_thread must call DELETE /v1/threads/{id}/workspace with the user's own bearer, because sandbox-manager refuses service principals for this RPC. This gates default-on.
An apply that races a reset can write a row whose blob the prefix delete has just removed, since uploads precede ApplyThreadWorkspaceChanges and no erasing marker is checked.

Corrected from the previous report: GET /v1/threads/{id}/workspace acquires a thread lease with no switch check in the gateway. With the switch off, AcquireLease takes the plain Create path (INSERT, no upsert), so the first GET leaves a live row and a second GET for the same user and thread inside the TTL fails on leases_thread_live_uq. Read from code, not run. The prune removes such rows only once the switch is on.

NEW: the prune covers thread-scoped rows only. Agent-scoped leases (one per Space run, released to DESTROYED at run end) keep their owner_id and are never pruned, so they accumulate with the user link. Their retention is an owner decision and needs its own predicate.

NEW: SnapshotSandbox does not refuse thread-scoped leases. BeginSnapshot exempts non-Space leases and snapshot.Store.Create has no scope check. Today's only caller (execution-core record_workspace_overlay) snapshots Space leases, so 'thread leases never have snapshots' holds for it but is not enforced. A snapshot row on a thread lease would survive the prune (no foreign key) with its object key. Refusing snapshots on thread leases in server.go is the fix; it is outside this round.
NEW: leases has no index on (scope_type, expires_at), so each pass scans the table. An index needs a migration number from section 4.4; none was added this round.
NEW: the acquire-versus-prune race relies on Postgres rechecking the predicate on a row an acquire slid forward (READ COMMITTED). The integration case covers the predicate matrix, not the race.
